notices.title: Boring under load.
notices.body: One failing host is set aside for a minute; the rest of the crawl goes on.
notices.cite: Scrapy, {month:breaker}: a circuit breaker for each host in stage 2.

notices.title: Raw before clean.
notices.body: Next month's question can't be known today, so the raw layer is appended to and never overwritten.
notices.cite: Scrapy, {month:delta}: raw pages written to Delta Lake with `write_deltalake`.

notices.title: Dashboards before speed.
notices.cite: Scrapy, {month:prometheus}: Prometheus metrics, then Grafana dashboards.

notices.title: Parse, don't pattern-match.
notices.body: A regex for a URL breaks on the first port or login inside it; `urllib.parse` does not.

notices.title: The surface is part of the system.
notices.body: A tool that confuses its operator is already failing.
notices.cite: This page, Nov 2025: its earlier editions read as a template.

rustmapper.header: Crawls a site and writes one line for every URL it finds.

entries.text: starts from your URL; by default also from sitemaps, certificate logs and Common Crawl

instead.text: starts from your URL; if asked, also from sitemaps, certificate logs and Common Crawl

entries.text: one queue per host, paced by that host's robots.txt
fetches pages, fewer at once when saves average over 500 ms; queues their links to your site, its subdomains and its parent domain
missing: release src/main.rs fn governor_task: contains 'current_permits > MIN_PERMITS'

instead.text: fetches up to 20 pages at a time from each host; queues their links to your site, its subdomains and its parent domain

entries.text: logged to disk, then saved to redb, every 50 ms

instead.text: logged to disk, then saved to redb, in batches

entries.text: {release} never exits by itself; done once `Received work item` is quiet for 30 s

instead.text: {release} never exits by itself, even after the last page

entries.text: press Ctrl-C once; a second press before `Saved to:` quits without writing the file
It sends requests with no pause between them, up to 256 at a time across all hosts. `--workers 1` sends one at a time.

instead.text: It sends requests with no pause unless the site's `robots.txt` sets a `Crawl-delay`, up to 256 at a time across all hosts. `--workers 1` sends one at a time.

entries.text: {release} ignores `Crawl-delay`, and asks for `robots.txt` only over https, so a plain-http site's rules are not read.
By default it asks crt.sh and Common Crawl about your domain. `--seeding-strategy none` asks no one.
It reads links from the HTML a server sends, and no JavaScript runs. go_go_go can render pages in headless Chrome.
{release} writes one `sitemap.xml` however many pages it found; the format allows 50,000 URLs per file.
{release} gives no `status_code` to a page that answers 404, 429 or 503, never asks for it again, and follows none of its links.
On main, a crawl stops by itself once the site runs out of pages: `tests/crawl_exits_when_idle.rs` passes in CI at `{head}`. That fix is not on PyPI yet.
